text: . Ahead of Independence Day, a platform for creative expression has been provided to the youth in Uttar Pradesh. For this, the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign was launched. Under this campaign, the graffiti wall programme organised near Lucknow University today. Artists from the city painted public murals on the theme of a mafia-free and changing Uttar Pradesh. Through these paintings, the Uttar Pradesh of before 2017 and the changes that have taken place in Uttar Pradesh thereafter were portrayed.On the wall, artists used their colours and imagination to portray in paintings the changed positive environment in the state in terms of law and order, infrastructure and opportunities for youth. Young painter Manish Saroj’s painting expressed the pain of Uttar Pradesh suffering under mafia rule before 2017, while also presenting a positive picture of the change taking place now.Under the campaign, a comic distribution and dialogue programme will be organised in Muzaffarnagar tomorrow. During this, an original comic based on communal harmony will be distributed. Along with this, dialogues will also be held with youth in schools. On August 14, the song ‘Azadi from Fear’ of the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign will be launched. It will also feature a confluence of rap, music and digital art.

. Thailand’s cabinet has approved an Education Ministry’s proposal to elevate school safety to a national agenda, following a mass shooting at a secondary school outside Bangkok last week that killed nine people.Deputy government spokesperson Patdarasm Thongsaluaykorn said, the move aims to strengthen prevention and response at educational institutions systematically, protecting children, teachers and education personnel nationwide. Under a ministry announcement effective immediately, Ms Patdarasm said all schools have been designated School Safety Zones and must set up centres for the protection of rights, liberties and safety on their premises. In a statement, she said the core of the approach is preventing risk before an incident occurs through strict searches and screening for weapons, illegal items and dangerous objects before entry, alongside mental health support systems covering both the physical and psychological welfare of students, teachers and staff.

. Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh today informed that around 440 space technology startups are registered in India. In a written reply in Lok Sabha, Dr Singh said Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre, IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities, NGEs to carry out various space activities. Out of these, 18 NGEs are start-ups. The Minister said the Government has undertaken several proactive measures following the liberalization of the space sector. This is being done to promote participation of startups in satellite manufacturing, launch services, downstream applications and space-based technologies. IN-SPACe is facilitating the transfer of available ISRO technologies to industry while also identifying and consolidating the technology requirements of industry for future technology development and transfer. Till date, 118 Technology Transfer Agreements have been executed.

. The Income Tax Department, as of the 10th of this month, has collected over 8.11 lakh crore rupees net direct tax for the financial year 2026-27 so far. It is 23.09 percent higher growth as compared to the financial year 2025-2026 during the same period. The collection includes corporate tax of over 2.70 lakh crore rupees and non-corporate tax of 5.07 lakh crore rupees.The department has also issued refunds of over one lakh 43 thousand crore rupees. The gross direct collection has recorded a significant growth of over 19 per cent, amounting to more than nine lakh 54 thousand crore rupees.
. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 10 paise to end at 95.33 rupees against the US dollar.

. Hungary’s parliament today elected former Supreme Court chief Andras Baka as the country’s next President. Baka, who will serve in the largely ceremonial role, was elected with the support of members of the governing centre-right Tisza party. Lawmakers from the opposition Fidesz party boycotted the vote and did not take part in the election. This decision marks Prime Minister Peter Magyar’s symbolic step to dismantle entrenched power structures built under former Prime Minister Viktor Orban.

. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowships and Awards for 2024 and 2025 on over 115 artists in a special investiture ceremony today in New Delhi. Union Minister of Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and Minister of State for Culture Rao Inderjit Singh will be present on the occasion.The Akademi Awards have been conferred since 1952. These honours not only symbolise the highest standard of excellence and achievement but also recognise sustained individual work and contribution. The honour of Akademi Fellow carries a purse money of three lakh rupees, while the Akademi Award carries a purse money of one lakh rupees besides a Tamrapatra and Angavastram.The Fellows and Awardees selected represent the nation as a whole and belong to different States and Union Territories. These eminent artists cover the entire gamut of the performing art forms expressed in the form of music, dance, drama, folk and tribal art, puppetry and allied theatre art forms.

. The death toll from the powerful earthquake that struck western Colombia yesterday has crossed 200 mark. Citing local authorities media reported that more than 200 people were killed and over 3,000 people are still missing. The death toll is expected to rise further as many are feared trapped under the rubble. Search and rescue operations are underway in western Colombia. The majority of the deaths were concentrated in the western cities of Cali, Pereira, Manizales, and Quibdo, where more than 100 buildings have collapsed. The 7.4 magnitude earthquake is one of the strongest to hit the South American country in decades.

. Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr L Murugan today said Government has established a Fact Check Unit in Press Information Bureau to mitigate fake news related to its programmes and policies. In a written reply in Lok Sabha, DR Murugan informed that the Fact Check Unit verifies claims relating to Government Ministries, Departments, PSUs and other Central Government organisations through a structured fact-checking process. It disseminates verified information through various platforms.The MoS further stated that Doordarshan and Akashvani further disseminate verified information through their news bulletins, programmes and digital platforms. DD News follows a multi-layered editorial mechanism involving rigorous fact-checking, cross-verification through multiple credible sources and editorial scrutiny before broadcast. PIB Fact Check content is regularly integrated into Doordarshan and Akashvani news and digital platforms to counter misinformation and false narratives.PIB, as the principal information dissemination agency of the Government, facilitates timely, credible and accurate communication in different forms through various media platforms. Prasar Bharati plays a key role in fulfilling the mandate of public service broadcasting. Information is disseminated in multiple languages, including regional languages and dialects, using various platforms.

. Lok Sabha today referred the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, to the Joint Parliamentary Committee for further scrutiny. The bill aims to further amend the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010. The objective of the Bill is to make the use of foreign contributions more transparent and accountable.Minister of State for Home Nityanand Rai moved the Bill to refer it to JPC comprising members of both the Houses for wider consultations. He said, the committee will consist of 21 members from the Lok Sabha, nominated by the Speaker, and 10 members from the Rajya Sabha, nominated by the Chairman. Mr Rai said, the Committee will submit its report to this House by the last day of the first week of the winter session.

. In Pakistan, 15 people, including women and children of a family, died after a three-wheeler vehicle fell into a canal due to over-speeding in Punjab province. The vehicle was carrying 26 wedding guests when it fell into the canal at Kot Addu in Muzaffargarh district of Punjab yesterday. A rescue operation was launched after three people swam through the canal and alerted the authorities. Police said, yesterday 12 bodies were recovered from the canal. Three more bodies were recovered today, taking the toll to 15.

. Philippine health authorities have issued an alert on water-borne diseases after floods hit the northern part of the country. The local health centre in the Ilocos region has warned residents of rising health risks as enhanced southwest monsoon rains continue to trigger flooding across the region. Residents were urged to guard against water-borne illnesses such as influenza, leptospirosis and dengue, which commonly spread during the rainy season.Red and yellow alerts were raised for power grids in central and southern Philippines today as several power plants remained unavailable.The Philippine National Police (PNP) has intensified post-disaster recovery efforts in the wake of tropical cyclones Luis and Maymay and the enhanced southwest monsoon. The PNP reported 26 weather-related fatalities till yesterday, including 25 civilians and one police officer.

. Global crude oil prices were displaying mixed trend today. Brent crude was trading 0.2 per cent down at 88 US dollars and 71 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading marginally up at 82 US dollars and 24 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. The Technology Development Board today signed an agreement with a private medical device company from Visakhapatnam for commercialisation of indigenous AI-Powered cervical cancer screening technology. The agreement will support the manufacturing and commercialization of GrivaVision, an indigenously developed, portable digital colposcope with AI-assisted capabilities for early detection of cervical pre-cancerous lesions. Through the Board’s support, the company will establish manufacturing capabilities at Kollam, Kerala, enabling commercial-scale production and wider deployment of the technology. The initiative seeks to make cervical cancer screening more accessible and affordable, particularly across primary and community healthcare settings. GrivaVision integrates a high-definition camera, an in-built display, user-friendly interface that assists gynaecologists in identifying pre-cancerous abnormalities during routine clinical examinations.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 0.4 per cent up at 1,53,419 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, Silver rose 0.8 per cent to 2,37, 214 rupees per kilogram.

. India’s retail inflation accelerated to 4.45 per cent on an annual basis in July, remaining above the Reserve Bank of India’s target of 4 per cent for the second consecutive month this year. The July inflation reading was moderately higher than the 4.38 per cent recorded in June as food prices remained elevated. The current print is the highest reading under the new 2024-base year Consumer Price Index (CPI) series.According to data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, inflation in rural areas increased to 4.84 per cent, while in urban regions it rose to 3.96 per cent. The food inflation rate, based on the All India Consumer Food Price Index, stood at 5.52 per cent last month, up from 5.32 per cent in the preceding month.According to the data, the increase in inflation in July was mainly attributed to rising prices in personal care, social protection, restaurants and accommodation services, food and beverages and intoxicants. The top items showing high inflation at the all India combined level included Silver, Gold, Diamond and Platinum Jewellery, Ginger, Garlic and Onion. In contrast, items with lowest inflation included Potato, Motor Car and Jeep, Lady’s finger, Peas, and Tomato.

. The Punjab and Haryana High Court has stayed the appointment process for the posts of 454 Pharmacy Officers over allegations of a paper leak in the recruitment. The examination for which was held on July 19th , this year. The posts were advertised by Baba Farid University of Health Sciences, Faridkot. The next hearing of the case has been scheduled on September 17.The stay orders of Punjab and Haryana High Court have come amid a political storm over the examination. Within a few hours of the alleged paper leak through high-tech pen cameras and other instruments, Punjab Police claimed to have busted an interstate cheating racket after its crackdown across 25 examination centres in three districts – Faridkot, Kotkapura and Ferozepur. The police arrested seven key conspirators and 28 candidates who were directly involved in this case.Since then, the Punjab government had been maintaining that the incident involved high-tech cheating rather than a conventional paper leak. However, this distinction has now become a major political flashpoint.Opposition parties including BJP, Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal have targeted the Aam Aadmi Party government and its leadership including the Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann for attempting to downplay the alleged paper leak as a minor cheating case. The opposition party leaders are demanding accountability.

. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey has urged the commodity market ecosystem to develop Indian benchmarks and good-delivery standards based on domestic market realities, instead of relying mainly on global benchmarks. Speaking at the Global Commodity Conclave 2026 in Mumbai today, he said the success of the commodity derivatives market should be judged by how effectively it helps the real economy discover prices and manage risks.Mr Pandey outlined four priorities namely making participation easier, widening the participant base, strengthening links with physical markets and investing in market education. SEBI is examining wider foreign portfolio investor (FPI) access to commodity indices and physically settled non-agricultural contracts. A consultation paper on FPI participation in exchange-traded commodity derivatives (ETCDs) was issued yesterday.He said consultation on position limits for agricultural commodities has been completed and guidelines will be issued shortly. SEBI chief also highlighted Project Jagrook, aimed at strengthening commodity market awareness among farmers, FPOs, MSMEs, hedgers and other market users. He said price differences in the Sensex and NSE have reduced significantly since 3rd August, following measures including indicative settlement prices displayed by major brokerages. The SEBI Chairman also cautioned about continuing losses in options trading, particularly on expiry days, and said a detailed analytical report on trader demographics and losses will be published shortly.

. The Calcutta High Court has cancelled OBC all certificates issued under the OBC-A and OBC-B classifications introduced by the previous Trinamool Congress government in West Bengal.A division bench of Justice Rajasekhar Mantha and Justice Anuj Singh yesterday while delivering the judgement said the two classifications no longer exist in the state and certificates issued under the earlier system have lost their validity. Holders of these certificates will now be treated as belonging to the general category.The controversy dates back to 2010, when the state divided OBC communities into OBC-A and OBC-B categories. In 2024, the High Court had struck down the inclusion of 66 communities in the OBC list and ordered a fresh survey.After the BJP government came to power in 2026, it abolished the OBC-A and OBC-B classification and introduced a single OBC category. The Suvendu Adhikari government also withdrew the previous administration’s challenge in the Supreme Court.With the legal challenge withdrawn, the earlier certificates lost their legal basis, leading to Wednesday’s High Court order.

. The Embassy of India in Nepal and various Nepali government bodies inked Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) for the execution of eight projects across the education, health and agriculture sectors utilising Indian grant aid. The eight developmental initiatives, carrying an estimated total value of 803 million Nepali rupees, are set to be executed via local government entities and institutions under the Government of Nepal.The Embassy stated that chosen under India’s High Impact Community Development Projects (HICDPs) framework, the schemes will be rolled out across diverse regions of the Himalayan nation. The agreements were signed between the Embassy of India in Kathmandu, Nepal’s Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, Federal Affairs and General Administration, alongside the designated project execution authorities of the Nepali administration. The Embassy of India noted that the ventures are intended to bolster progress in key priority areas, encompassing health, education and agriculture.

. The FIH Hockey Men’s and Women’s World Cup 2026 will feature a revamped competition structure, with the traditional quarterfinal stage scrapped and the top two teams from each of the two crossover pools advancing directly to the semi-finals. Belgium and the Netherlands jointly host the tournament from August 15 to 30. The new format means teams will have little margin for error from the outset, with results from the opening pool stage potentially carrying over into the next phase. India’s men have been drawn alongside England, Pakistan and Wales in Pool D, while the Indian women will face China, England and South Africa in their Pool D campaign.The tournament will begin with the 16 teams in each competition split across four pools of four. From August 15 to 20, every team will play three matches against the other sides in its pool, with the final standings determining the composition of the next phase. The top two teams from Pools A and D will move into Pool E, while the leading two teams from Pools B and C will form Pool F. The top two finishers from Pool E and Pool F will advance directly to the last four. The women’s tournament will conclude in the Netherlands on August 29, with the bronze-medal match followed by the final. The men’s World Cup will conclude in Belgium a day later, on August 30, with its bronze-medal match and final.

. Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that saree is not merely a piece of attire, rather a magnificent symbol of Indian culture. The Minister said this in a video message during Saree Shastra in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat underlined the mastery of wearing one saree in multiple ways, the craft of designing and weaving a single saree in diverse styles. Highlighting the tradition of representing culture through sarees, he said that exhibitions and events like this help spread awareness about India’s tradition of wearing and weaving sarees, and understanding which saree suits which occasion far and wide.Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Khadse said that the exhibition serves as a prime example of presenting diverse states and culture through sarees. The Minister said that the exhibition brings together artists from across the country and aims to present their work through the medium of the saree. He said, it reflects the country’s rich culture, which is being conveyed through saree craftsmanship.Saree Shastra is a three-day exhibition to honour the women who weave, preserve and wear sarees. The event reimangines the saree as one of India’s most enduring cultural artefact.

. On World Elephant Day, Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupender Yadav, today said that Project Elephant reflects India’s commitment to protecting elephants, conserving their habitats and promoting harmonious coexistence between elephants and communities. In a social media post, Mr Yadav said that under Project Elephant, various measures are being implemented, including early warning systems and AI-based alerts to keep communities informed, solar-powered fences and trenches to protect people and elephants, and timely compensation for crop losses suffered by farmers. He added that the railways are also adopting warning signals, AI-based solutions and speed restrictions in critical corridors to prevent elephant deaths. The Minister also said that the government is promoting education and awareness to encourage communities to live in harmony with elephants.

. In Canadian Open Tennis, the men’s and women’s semi-final lineups are officially locked in.. In Women’s Singles, seventh-seeded Iga Swiatek of Poland take on ninth seed Elina Svitolina of Ukraine in Toronto for a place in final. Swiatek routed fifteenth-seeded Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 while  Svitolina  defeated Ekaterina Alexandrova of Russia 3-6, 6-0, 6-3 in the quarterfinal.In another semifinal,  Elena Rybakina will meet fourth seed Coco Gauff in the semi-finals in Toronto tomorrow morning. The Kazakh, Rybakina defeated 11th-seed Naomi Osaka 4-6,7-6, 6-4 to advance to last four. Gauff reached the last four after the American received a walkover in her quarter-final when her opponent Belinda Bencic of Switzerland withdrew due to a hip injury.Spanish teenager Rafael Jodar will face American Brandon Nakashima in the Men’s Singles semi-finals at Montreal, early morning tomorrow.The 19-year-old Jodar is on course to break the record for the fastest rise into the top 10 of Men’s Singles after beating Arthur Filis in the quarter-finals.In the other semifinal, defending Canadian Open champion and fifth seed Ben Shelton will face fellow American Learner Tien.

. The Rail Coach Factory, Kapurthala, in Punjab, is rolling out the first rake comprising 19 LHB broad gauge passenger coaches for Bangladesh Railways today. The rake comprises 03 AC Sleeper Cars, 03 AC Chair Cars, 11 Non-AC Chair Cars and 02 Power Cars.These coaches incorporate several unique design features and modifications, many of which have been developed for the first time in such type of coaches. The coaches have been specially customised to meet the operational and passenger requirements of Bangladesh Railway.The seating arrangement incorporates specially designed reclining chairs with stainless steel armrests and stainless-steel footrests, offering multiple reclining positions for enhanced passenger comfort. They also have an integrated CCTV surveillance system, a passenger alarm system, a Baby Care Room and a Prayer Room. The association between RCF, Kapurthala and Bangladesh Railway began with the successful supply of 120 LHB broad gauge passenger coaches during 2015-16.

. India will host the first Global South Film Festival next year. It was announced today at a press conference held on the sidelines of the BRICS WAVES Bazaar in Mumbai. Several agreements aimed at strengthening international cooperation in the film and entertainment sector were also announced.Organisations including the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) signed agreements, exchanged Letters of Intent and held talks with partner institutions from countries including Brazil, Russia and Vietnam. The participating organisations also agreed to explore opportunities for film co-production.The two-day WAVES BRICS Bazaar, which opened in Mumbai yesterday, concludes this evening. Prakash Magdum, Managing Director of the NFDC, said the initiative brought together more than 900 delegates from the 20 BRICS member and partner countries. Around 250 meetings were held during the one-and-a-half-day event, providing a platform for government agencies, entertainment industry professionals, investors and content creators to exchange ideas and explore opportunities for collaboration.

. The Ministry of Textiles will organise ‘Srijan: Voices from the Loom’, a special gathering celebrating the women behind India’s handlooms and recognising their inspiring journeys, voices and contributions to the weaving heritage of the country. The programme will be held in New Delhi today.Secretary of the Ministry of Textiles Neelam Shami Rao will attend the programme. The Ministry said that during the session, over hundred women weavers from 6 handloom clusters will share their stories of Resilience, Creativity and Role in preserving India’s Weaving Traditions. An anthology featuring the inspiring stories, journeys and voices of these women weavers will also be released on the occasion.

. India has made a strong start at the U-23 Commonwealth Fencing Championship in Lagos, Nigeria, winning 17 medals, including 4 gold, on the opening day. The Indian contingent has secured 4 gold, 4 silver and 9 bronze medals at the championship, which began on Sunday. Indian fencers reached the podium in all 6 individual events across the Sabre, Foil and Epee disciplines.In the men’s Sabre event, Nikhil Wagh won the gold medal, while Lakshay Badser secured silver. Ashwini Arya and Laishram Moramba bagged bronze medals. In men’s Foil, Tejas Patil won silver and Hemash Sanasam secured bronze. In men’s Epee, Lokesh Vemani claimed silver, while Shaurya Ashwini and Godwin Anbkess won bronze.In the women’s events, Joys Ashita clinched gold in Foil, with teammate Kanaglakshmi winning silver. Prachi Lohan won gold in women’s Epee, while Nivedhya Nair and Anupriya secured bronze medals. In women’s Sabre, Jeferlin bagged gold, Aakhari won silver and Shreya Gupta took bronze.India will look to build on its strong opening-day performance in the remaining events of the championship.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that public capital should act as a catalyst for private investment, rather than a substitute for it. Addressing a seminar in Jaipur on the role of the New Development Bank in mobilising private capital in BRICS member countries, Mrs. Sitharaman said BRICS economies are among the major engines of global growth, but they also face challenges in attracting private capital.She said that besides ensuring the availability of capital, it is equally important to build investor confidence, maintain stability and provide a predictable, long-term policy framework.The Finance Minister highlighted the role of multilateral development banks in reducing investment risks, making projects more financially viable and strengthening investor confidence, thereby helping mobilise private capital on a larger scale.Referring to India’s experience, Mrs. Sitharaman said the Central Government has strengthened the country’s infrastructure through sustained public capital expenditure and structural reforms.New Development Bank President Dilma Rousseff also addressed the seminar.Earlier, Economic Affairs Secretary Anuradha Thakur said that increasing private capital participation is an important need in the current economic environment.The seminar is being held as part of the BRICS Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors’ meeting in Jaipur under India’s BRICS Chairship 2026, with the objective of strengthening cooperation on global economic and financial issues.

. Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa defeated Javokhir Sindarov in a second-round match of the Sinquefield Cup in St Louis, United States. It is his first victory in the tournament, which is the penultimate event of the Grand Chess Tour. Praggnanandhaa dominated the game from start to finish. He slowly pressed his advantage in the endgame, which arose from a queen pawn opening.Sindarov chose an endgame that was equal and should have ended in a draw. But he could not match Praggnanandhaa’s determination. The Indian kept pressing and eventually turned the drawn position into a winning one. The game lasted 95 moves. With this victory, Praggnanandhaa moved to 1.5 points from two games.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended with modest losses today. The Sensex dipped 188 points or 0.24 per cent to close at 77,966. The Nifty dropped 36 points or 0.15 to settle at 24,436.In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained 0.3 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index fell 0.2 per cent.

. Indian weightlifter Maharajan Arumugapandian clinched the silver medal in the men’s 65 kg category at the Asian Junior Weightlifting Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan today.Maharajan produced a new personal best total of 285 kilograms, lifting 128 kg in the snatch and 157 kg in the clean and jerk to secure silver. Vietnam’s Hoang Thach claimed the gold medal with a total lift of 291 kilograms, finishing six kilograms ahead of Maharajan.

. Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi chaired a meeting of senior officials of the Ministry. In a social media post, Mr. Joshi stated that the meeting was convened to discuss the proposal to continue the ‘National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme’ from the financial years 2026-27 to 2030-31. Discussions during the meeting focused on the key aspects of the scheme and its continued implementation to support students across the country.

. Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi has informed that no decision has been taken by the Government to increase ethanol blending with petrol beyond 20 percent. In a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha, Mr Gopi said that any future decision regarding higher ethanol blends will be taken only after detailed scientific and technical studies and consultations with all relevant stakeholders, including automobile manufacturers and Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).The Minister said that the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile manufacturers, OMCs  and technical institutions.He said, extensive laboratory studies and field trials covering parameters such as engine durability, emissions and fuel efficiency, have confirmed that E20 is safe for use under prescribed standards. The Minister added that these studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. The Minister said, these extensive laboratory studies, field validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel.

. The Sports Ministry today suspended its recognition of the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI)and asked the Indian Olympic Association to form an ad-hoc committee to administer the sport, citing governance deficiencies within TTFI. In its order, the Ministry cited TTFI’s failure to conduct elections on time as one of the reasons for the suspension after getting an unsatisfactory response to a show cause notice issued earlier. The Ministry stated that the IOA, in consultation with the international body (ITTF) will take appropriate action to create an internal regulatory mechanism, including the constitution of an ad-hoc committee, till such time that a duly constituted governance structure is restored in TTFI.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah launched the Gramin Gyan Setu app through video conferencing yesterday. The app has been developed to integrate libraries in the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency of Gujarat.Speaking on the occasion, Mr Shah said the app was launched on the birth anniversary of Padma Shri S R Ranganathan, observed as National Library Day. He said the objective is to establish a library in every village, preferably near schools, to encourage children to read and learn.Mr Shah said around 63 village libraries have already been established, while 7 hundred 52 libraries are now connected through the app. He said four libraries, together having around two lakh 80 thousand books, have been linked with the rural libraries. He said vans, arranged through his MP Local Area Development funds, will visit villages every fortnight to collect issued books and deliver books requested through the app.The Home Minister said the initiative will provide children in villages access to a much larger collection of books. He emphasised the importance of reading and guidance from competent librarians in shaping young minds and developing responsible citizens. He also urged families, including housewives, to make productive use of their spare time by acquiring knowledge and encouraging children to study.

. The Fourth Session of the India-Namibia Joint Trade Committee (JTC) concluded in New Delhi today. The session which began yesterday, was led by Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Amit Kumar from the Indian side while the Namibian delegation was led by the Namibian Executive Director, Ministry of International Relations and Trade Ndiitah Nghipondoka-Robiati. The agreed minutes of the Session were signed by the two Co-Chairs today.The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that during the meeting, both sides underlined the need to move bilateral trade beyond a raw-material-based composition towards value addition within Namibia, and to translate discussions into concrete mechanisms with defined timelines and assigned responsibilities. The Ministry added that the bilateral merchandise trade between India and Namibia rose to over 592 million dollars in 2025-26 from 568 million dollars in 2024-25.

. Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha produced a superb comeback to win the Korea Masters 2026, beating China’s Han Qian Xi in the women’s singles final this morning. The Assam shuttler recovered from losing the opening game to prevail 14-21, 21-14, and 21-14 in 53 minutes and claim her first BWF title. Earlier, Ashmita reached the final after defeating fellow Indian Rakshitha Ramraj 21-13, 16-21, 21-13 in the semifinal yesterday. While Han outplayed South Korea’s G Kim 22-20, 18-21, and 21-14 in the other semifinal to advance to the final. Ashmita Chaliha had won the gold medal at the 2024 Asia Team Championships. At the 2019 South Asian Games, she had secured gold medals in both the women’s singles and team events.

. In the World Athletics U20 Championships, India enjoyed a historic day in Eugene, USA, with Basant Kumar Meghwal and Shahnavaz Khan becoming the first Indians to win medals in the high jump and long jump at the championships. Basant Kumar Meghwal, the reigning Asian U20 champion, won silver in the men’s high jump with a personal best clearance of 2.21 metres. Shahnavaz Khan claimed bronze in the men’s long jump with a best effort of 7.84 metres.Algeria’s Younes Ayachi won the high jump gold, while Great Britain’s Otis Poole took bronze. The two medals took India’s tally at the championships to three. India have now equalled their medal haul from the 2021 and 2022 editions.

. A former US Marine, Robert Gilman, who had been imprisoned by Russia for over four years, has been freed on humanitarian grounds and is due to return home after advocates raised concerns about his health. Announcing Gilman’s release in a post on Truth Social, President Donald Trump said he spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin, who agreed to release him on humanitarian grounds.Trump said he appreciated the decision and the fact that Russia did not ask for a prisoner swap or exchange. Trump said Gilman was imprisoned in Russia during former US President Joe Biden’s administration in 2022. He said Gilman, who served in the US Marines from August 2019 until August 2020, was travelling by train when he was arrested in January 2022 in Voronezh.According to Russian media, Gilman was detained for allegedly kicking a police officer while drunk. However, his father said the charges were false. Gilman had been one of at least 10 Americans known to be imprisoned in Russia. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also thanked Russia and vowed to bring home all other detained Americans.

. Lok Sabha has passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026. When the House met at 3:00 PM after the second adjournment, Union Coal and Mines Minister G Kishan Reddy moved the Bill to further amend the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. The bill aims to make India’s mining sector more efficient, investment-friendly and well-equipped to fulfil the country’s growing demand for critical minerals. The Bill was passed without discussion amid opposition uproar.

. Parliament has passed the National Co-operative Development Corporation(NCDC) (Amendment) Bill, 2026 with Rajya Sabha approving it today. Lok Sabha has already passed the Bill. Minister of State for Cooperation Murlidhar Mohol moved the bill, which aims to further amend the National Co-operative Development Corporation Act, 1962. The Bill allows the Corporation to undertake its activities in industrial goods. The legislation also allows the state governments to extend funding from the Corporation to any entity engaged in co-operative development. The Corporation can also provide loans and grants directly to any co-operative society or entity engaged in co-operative development.Replying to discussion, Mr Mohol said that through this Bill, the welfare and economic empowerment of crores of farmers across the country will be strengthened. He noted that NCDC, was established to provide financial assistance for the organised and sustained development of the cooperative sector in the country. The Minister highlighted that from the establishment of NCDC in 1963 until 2014, the previous government provided financial assistance of only around 45 thousand crore rupees. He, however, said, in the last 12 years since 2014, financial assistance has increased to around four lakh crore rupees.The Minister highlighted that India’s cooperative sector is among the largest cooperative networks in the world. Mr Mohol said that today, the country has more than eight lakh cooperative societies, with around 30 crore members associated with them. He informed that 80 thousand Primary Agricultural Credit Societies, PACS, are being computerised and have been enabled to undertake around 25 different types of business activities. The Minister informed that Tribhuvan Sahkari University has been established to provide trained and skilled manpower to the cooperative sector. Mr Mohol said that through this institution, around 17 lakh young people will be trained over the next five years and will contribute to the cooperative sector. He said, more than 163 major initiatives have been undertaken in the cooperative sector in just last five years.

. The Report of the Inquiry Committee investigating allegations concerning former Allahabad High Court Judge Yashwant Varma was tabled in both the Houses of Parliament. In the Lok Sabha, Secretary General Uttpal Kuma Singh tabled the Hindi and English versions of the Report of the Inquiry Committee constituted under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 as well as the Oral and documentary evidence recorded during the course of the inquiry. While in the Rajya Sabha, the report in this regard was tabled by Secretary General P C Mody.The Judges Inquiry Committee, investigating allegations concerning Yashwant Varma, had submitted its report to the Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla in May this year. The Committee was constituted by Mr Birla on 12th of August last year to probe the allegations levelled against Justice Varma, after a sum of burnt cash was found at his official residence in New Delhi.

The Indian fencing team collected three gold, one silver, and one bronze medal across various senior individual events on the third day of the Commonwealth Championship at Lagos in Nigeria today.Team India’s stellar day three performance brought the nation’s overall combined medal count to an extraordinary 29 medals, comprising 8 Gold, 7 Silver, and 14 Bronze.India established immediate dominance in the Senior Women’s Foil category, securing a gold-silver victory. Kanaglakshmi captured the gold medal following a precise and controlled campaign, while teammate Joys Ashitha took silver to claim the top two spots on the podium ahead of England’s Georgia Green and Emily Goodchild, who won Bronze.The success continued in the Senior Men’s Epee discipline, where Rajendran Shanthimol Sherjin put on a commanding display to secure country’s second gold medal of the day. Sherjin outpointed South Africa’s Kruger Pieter, who finished with silver, while Wales’ Burkhardt Marc and South Africa’s Losevsky Sergey shared the bronze medals.In the Senior Men’s Sabre event, Singh Karan Singh clinched India’s third gold medal of the day with an outstanding final fight against Australia’s Shim Yoongi, who took silver.Teammate Kumaresan Padma Gisho Nidhi added to the medal haul by winning bronze alongside Nigeria’s Akinyosoye Oluwafolayemi.
